messages:
alex: Quick brain dump — I'd like to propose we separate model binding granularity into three explicit scopes: global, route, and component. The idea: route bindings let product teams pick a model for a URL/endpoint; component bindings let us mix-and-match submodels (embedder vs generator vs ranker) per route. Pros: very flexible rollouts and cheaper fallbacks. Cons: more metadata and resolver complexity. Thoughts?

maria: Sounds promising. One immediate question: how do we signal deprecation and compatibility when components diverge? e.g., gen-v2 changes tokenization slightly. We need a soft-deprecate+compat band in the schema so clients/resolvers can make informed fallbacks.

sam: Re: resolver complexity — clients doing naive pin-by-model-id will break. We should add a resolver output that flattens component bindings into an "effective_model_id" per route, and include provenance so clients can opt into the new granularity. Maybe a migration flag.

kevin: From an ops perspective we also need a concrete migration/playbook. Proposal: 1) Add component binding alongside existing route/global binding (no overwrite). 2) Deploy canary at route level (5%, 1h). 3) Monitor latency + quality evals (prompt set) + error rate. 4) If regression -> automatic fallback to route/global effective id. Also need a small backfill job to populate new bindings for active tenants.

alex: Example lightweight schema snippet to discuss (not final):
```json
{
  "binding": {
    "scope": "route",
    "route": "/search",
    "components": {
      "embedder": "m-embed-v2",
      "generator": "m-gen-v1"
    },
    "deprecation": {
      "soft": true,
      "soft_until": "2025-06-01",
      "compat_range": ">=1.0 <2.0",
      "breaking_change": false
    }
  }
}
```

maria: I like the compat_range field. Also suggest we add a telemetry hint: `stability_score` (0-1) so rollout tooling can prefer higher-stability variants automatically.

sam: For client compatibility: can we add a `resolved_id` header the resolver returns, plus `binding_version` so clients know if they should re-resolve? Example header: `X-Redwood-Resolved-Model: m-gen-v1; binding-v=20250312`. That avoids clients caching an old composite mapping forever.

kevin: Agree. Ops responsibilities: create `redwoodctl model bind --scope component|route|global` and a migration helper `redwoodctl model migrate-bindings --dry-run` (backfill + detect conflicts). Also add an automated canary job that enforces our thresholds. I'll draft the runbook and CLI RFC.

alex: A couple of edge cases: - tenant overrides (tenant wants custom embedder) — allow tenant-level component bindings but block global forced-deprecation until tenant adoption window closes. - partial compatibility: one component is breaking, the other is fine — need per-component soft_deprecate to avoid blanket rollbacks.

maria: On deprecation windows: suggest default 90 days soft window for non-breaking API changes, 30 days for patch fixes, and immediate for security/PII issues. Make windows configurable per binding.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary created for /search with components {embedder:m-embed-v2, generator:m-gen-v1} at 5% traffic. Canary id=canary-17777. Monitoring: latency, error-rate, eval-run-1 active.

sam: Who will own the schema migration? @kevin for ops + @maria for API semantics? We should also list clients that need update: mobile SDK (caching), server SDK (resolver + header), and console (UI to edit component bindings).

alex: OK — next steps: I'll open a short RFC PR with the schema draft, include the snippet above and a migration checklist. @kevin please attach the ops playbook and a proposed `redwoodctl` surface. @maria please add compatibility semantics + default windows. If anyone wants to sketch the resolver response format, drop it in the PR. :thumbsup:
